models.observations: At 48 px the straw vault makes a low golden arch above the timber hearth. Its generous overhang, small side light, raked stone feet and tucked-in chimney give the house a different profile from the hipped Dawn variant. Both reduced GLBs keep the characteristic roof and front step. The 355/196/80 triangle meshes passed serialized checks. The pot and the amber wall lamp lack contact with their supports.
defects: LOD0. Lower the entire doorway pot by 0.008 tile. The bottom rim sits at y=0.008 above bare ground.

LOD0/1. The back of the amber lamp socket clears the timber by approximately 0.013/0.011 tile along its centreline. Add a solid mounting block that enters the wall batter and connects to the existing socket.

models.observations: The tall off-centre flue, hipped roof and little straw-roofed side room define this house at 48 px. The small bench, amber lamp and thick stone foot bring scale to the timber front. The side-window hood emerges as a small dark peg through the lighter annex thatch. The 351/174/90 triangle meshes passed serialized checks. Comparing front and rear LODs shows the entire tall flue disappearing at the first transition.
defects: Preserve the tall flue in LOD1 and LOD2 as a simple tapered shaft with a cap. Keep its height and attachment on the rear roof pitch so the roof outline holds through the transition.
LOD0. Move the side window and hood to the exposed opposite wall. Their current position puts the window inside the side room and leaves the end of its hood sticking through the annex thatch.
LOD0. Lower the pot and its contents by 0.008 tile to place the lowest rim on the ground.
LOD0/1. Bridge the approximately 0.013 tile gap behind the amber lamp with a mounting block running into the tapered timber front.

models.observations: The clipped roof and smaller copper-trimmed upper tier form a broad, stepped silhouette at 48 px. Ochre masonry, the chunky front lintel, a gilded chimney rim and the diamond lamp distinguish this Bronze home from the straw Dawn vault. Both lower LODs preserve the two tiers, the step and the stone foot. The 407/254/102 triangle meshes passed serialized checks. The lamp has a measurable air gap behind it, and the pot floats just clear of the ground.
defects: LOD0/1. Extend a mounting block from the rear of the diamond socket into the ochre wall. The centreline gaps are 0.0275 and 0.0253 tile respectively.
LOD0. Drop the complete pot by 0.008 tile so its lowest ring reaches terrain.

models.observations: The ochre barrel roof and low copper-edged room make two clearly unequal volumes at 48 px. A bright lintel, jewel lamp and small flue lead the eye to the domestic entrance. The window hood crosses the copper-edged annex as an isolated brown tab. Both lower meshes retain the side room and vault. The 453/292/120 triangle meshes passed serialized checks.
defects: LOD0. Relocate the side-window assembly to a clear wall. The annex encloses the pane and cuts across its hood, leaving a stray projection on the annex roof.
LOD0/1. Seat the amber lamp on a solid bracket. Its central gap to the wall measures 0.0284 tile at full detail and 0.0271 tile at the middle LOD.
LOD0. Lower the pot by 0.008 tile as one assembly to give the bottom rim ground contact.

models.observations: The dark timber vault, metal hoop and fieldstone front make the Iron progression legible beside the Bronze house at 48 px. The low chimney tucked along the crown and tiny hooded side light give the broad, buttressed hall a residential scale. All three GLBs keep the vaulted roof, stove flue and entry. The 387/234/100 triangle meshes passed serialized checks. Contact is missing behind the lamp and beneath the pot.
defects: LOD0/1. Extend a bracket into the stone behind the amber lamp. Its socket centre is separated from the wall face by 0.0144/0.0121 tile.
LOD0. Ground the pot by lowering the entire assembly by 0.008 tile.

models.observations: The taller main vault and low slate side vault give this house an asymmetric two-arch silhouette at 48 px. The warm lintel and doorway lamp stand out against the stone, and the dark chimney remains visible in both reduced meshes. The full-detail side window occupies the wall within the annex. The 437/276/126 triangle meshes passed serialized checks.
defects: LOD0. Move the hidden hooded window to the clear wall opposite the slate annex. A section through the hood centre places it inside the annex roof.
LOD0/1. Add a mounting block behind the diamond lamp. Its socket clears the fieldstone wall by about 0.015 tile at both levels.
LOD0. Lower the complete doorway pot by 0.008 tile so the lowest ring rests on the ground.

models.observations: The golden thatch vault still defines the Dawn hearth at 48 px. The little chimney persists above the roof in both reduced rear views, and the steps meet a substantial timber doorway. The pot rim rests at y=0. The diamond socket extends 0.0574 tile into the front timber in LOD0 and 0.0593 in LOD1. The 387/238/112 triangle exports cleared serialized, winding and exposed-pair checks.

At thumbnail size the leaning flue rises distinctly above the main hip. All three exported LODs preserve its height and cap in both views. The pale thatch on the annex now reads as one clean slope. The hooded window and rear vent are visible on the other side, while the bench stays beside the entrance. The pot base measures y=0 and the lamp back seats at least 0.057 tile inside the timber on both lamp-bearing LODs. The 383/216/122 triangle meshes cleared validation.

The broad stepped cap, gold upper course and small stove chimney remain distinct together at phone size and in both distance meshes. Thick buttresses step out from under the ochre eaves. The lamp is seated 0.0429/0.0451 tile into the wall at LOD0/1, and the pot stands on the ground beside the stair. All three exported levels cleared the validator at 439/266/134 triangles.

The low annex has a clean copper-edged roof beneath the higher ochre vault. Its opposite wall carries the hooded lamp window, visible beside the stone buttress from the rear. All three levels retain the two roof masses and the small capped flue. The front socket reaches 0.0420/0.0433 tile into the wall at the two relevant distances. The doorstep pot reaches y=0. The 485/304/152 triangle exports cleared validation.

At 48 px the dark timber arc and stone entrance distinguish this lodge from the lighter Bronze homes. Front and rear distance views keep the vault, plinth and capped flue. The doorway pot now sits at ground level and the diamond light has a positive mounting depth of 0.0560/0.0583 tile. The 419/246/112 triangle GLBs cleared the serialized and exposed-surface checks.

The two unequal vaults are clear at 48 px and survive both reductions. In reverse view the hooded side window can now be seen between the buttresses on the open wall. The slate annex, iron hoop and warm doorway retain their separate values. The pot rim reaches y=0. The lamp socket extends 0.0553/0.0550 tile into the stone front. The 469/288/138 triangle exports cleared validation at all levels.

rounds.inspection: Inspected every listed asset’s authored age previews at phone scale, rendered all three serialized LODs at 64 px and inspected LOD1 at two angles. Compared neutral 64 px renders of all available eras in each audited family. Verified fragment metadata, shared material and atlas, triangle budgets and ratios, surface findings, orientation and local shape duplication against the reviewed files.

models.observations: The stepped hip roof has a low raised cap and a projecting square flue. Heavy corner buttresses frame a short stair and dark recessed door. These hold the Bronze house together in both side views at LOD1.

The long round-backed roof, offset side room and square chimney distinguish the second Bronze house from the stepped-cap version. The broad roof lands on intact walls and the short stair reaches the door at LOD1.

The strapped vault projects forward over a squared-off stone gable, while an attached lower vault flanks the main door. Both roofs and the entrance surround hold their shapes at LOD1. A warm lamp separates the entrance from the dark iron.

The single low straw-covered vault sits on splayed supports, with one small roof opening and a sheltered front door. The warm roof dominates at phone size. The middle mesh keeps the supports and broad entrance stair.

rounds.critic: Independent visual critic, frozen middle-LOD fidelity review
rounds.inspection: Inspected current age previews and all three serialized LODs at phone scale. Examined the middle mesh from the front, side and rear at larger scale and compared individual entrances and surfaces against LOD0. Rechecked the serialized catalog metadata, triangle ratios, exposed surfaces and shell orientation. Existing design scores were retained for unchanged designs that remained legible.

models.observations: The vault, low side annex, porch steps and supported corner walls stay complete when the loose barrel disappears. The roof-to-gable joins remain solid from behind.
The two strapped roof sections, attached annex and stone entry frame stay in place. Rear and side views show a complete stone shell between the buttresses.
The broad straw vault still spans both brown gables. Its squat supports and dark timber door remain intact after the small barrel is omitted.

rounds.critic: RC6 independent housing, town center and Saurian civic critic
rounds.inspection: Compared all sibling entries at 64 px in paint and in both unpainted cameras. Inspected every changed age preview, all three serialized LODs, and reverse views of the middle model. Compared the same-age house alternatives side by side and examined the three races together. Recomputed the picture and directional corner metrics, verified the package metadata and GLB statistics, and checked the actual serialized surfaces and shell orientations for each changed model.

models.observations: The broad ochre slab, box lookout and square side workshop leave a stepped outline above the open doorstep. The stone patio and workshop block stay present at the last LOD. The double-domed Bronze alternative occupies a markedly different volume.
Two bronze half-domes of different diameters sit beside a straight porched entry. That roof grouping reads from either native grayscale corner and survives the coarser facets of LOD2.

The striped, tapering stone beehive and low rectangular door hood have a continuous outline through all LODs. The blunt summit, slit window and heavy foot distinguish it from the Bronze twin domes and from the steep Iron gable.
The tall slate pitch and low side hood make the longer Iron dwelling legible. A capped masonry flue rises above the far roof pitch at LOD0. Both simplified views leave the entire pitch bare.
defects: Retain the capped flue as a low-sided chimney at LOD1 and LOD2. Its silhouette and attachment to the rear roof plane are visible from both viewing directions.

rounds.critic: RC6 independent housing and Saurian civic critic, corrected candidate review
rounds.inspection: Compared the published painted age previews and family sheets against the original holds and named lookalikes. Rendered both unpainted 64 px views independently from each of the three actual LOD meshes. Inspected the native family cameras and the larger multi-camera LOD sheet. Recomputed same-family picture likeness and directional corner overlap, checked the fragment against the GLB and verified all three serialized levels for exposed coplanar faces and inverted shells.

models.observations: The square flue and projecting cap now rise above the same rear roof plane in all three meshes. The shaft is visible end-on as well as from behind. Its sharp slate gable and low side hood remain distinct from the newly parapeted Medieval v1.
